3  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1)OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988, PRAYING TO CALL FOR THE LOWER COURT RECORDS IN THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 02.02.2022 PASSED IN MVC NO.373/2020 ON THE FILE OF THE II ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL-II, BALLARI,
AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION BY MODIFYING THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD FROM RS.31,34,000/- TO RS.60,25,000/-.
 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
BASAVARAJA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Both cases arising out of judgment and award dated 02nd February, 2022 passed in MVC No.373 of 2020 passed by II Additional District and Sessions Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XII,
Ballary (for short, hereinafter referred to as "Tribunal").
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties in these appeals are referred to with their rank and status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the petition are that on 07th January, 2020 at about 2.45 pm deceased Prabhakara while was proceeding as pillion rider on motorcycle bearing No.KA-16/EH- 2839 near Kunta Maramma Temple, Sulenahalli, Molakalmuru taluk, Chitradurga District, at that time, the driver of bus NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB bearing Registration No.KA-16/B-1105 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident, due to which Prabhakar sustained grievous injuries and succumbed at the spot.
The body was shifted to Government Hospital, Molakalmuru where the postmortem was conducted.
It is further contended that the deceased was hale and healthy prior to accident, was aged about 21 years and was pursuing B.Com final year.

It is further contended that the deceased was doing water-curing to newly coming up buildings and was earning Rs.600/- a day and due to his untimely death, the family has lost the earning member of their family.
It is also contended that the accident in question had taken place due to negligent act on the part of respondent No.1-driver of the offending bus.

Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.3 being the insurer of the said vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and hence had preferred the claim petition.
4. Pursuant to issuance of notice, respondents 1 and 3 appeared and filed their written statement.

Respondent No.2 did not appear and was placed ex-parte.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB 5.

The gist of the written statement of respondent No.1 is that the driver of the bus was driving slowly and cautiously and the accident happened due to the negligent act of the rider of motorcycle D P Rudraiah S/O Dodda Palaiah vs Alla Baksha S/O Sabjan Sab on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99900340/
4 itself and hence respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation and accordingly sought for dismsisal of the appeal.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The substance of statement of respondent No.3 is that the driver of the bus was driving slowly on the proper side of the road, it is the rider of the motorcycle who came in a rash and negligent manner and has contributed to the accident.
It is also contended that the rider of the motorcycle was not having driving licence and the motorcycle was also not insured.

Though the accident is out of collusion between bus and the motorcycle, the owner or the insurer of the motorcycle are not made parties to the petition and hence for non-joinder of necessary parties to the petition, the petition is bad in law and accordingly, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

7. Based on the rival pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues for its consideration:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on the alleged date, time and place, respondent No.1 being the driver of the offended vehicle, drove it in high speed, with rash and negligent manner, dashed to the deceased R. Prabhakara, due to that, he sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what extent, from whom?
3. What order or award?
8.
In order to substantiate their case, Petitioner No.1 got himself examined as PW1 and got marked 13 documents as Exhibits P1 to P13.
On behalf of respondents, respondent No.3 was examined as RW1 and got marked two documents as Exhibits R1 and R2.
9. In view of the above finding, Tribunal allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.31,34,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB award the Insurance Company has preferred MFA No.102193 of 2022 questioning the liability as well as the quantum of compensation; and claimants have preferred MFA No.102453 of 2022 seeking enhancement of compensation.

5 10. Heard Sri G.N. Raichur, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-Insurance Company and Sri Gurukumar V.A., learned counsel appearing for the claimants.

11. Sri G.N. Raichur, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in saddling the liability on the Insurance in spite of the defence and evidence on record that the rider of motorcycle was riding the same without having driving licence and the motorcycle was also not insured.
He further submits that the Tribunal ought to have exonerated the appellant from the liability.

It is also contended that the Tribunal has committed an error in taking the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month in spite of petitioners have not produced any documentary proof in support of the income.

The learned counsel further contended that the Investigating Officer submitted charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle NC:
2023:KHC-D:10953-DB which is not considered by the Tribunal.
Hence, on all these grounds, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.
12. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased.
It is submitted that the deceased was earning Rs.600/- per day by doing water- curing to the newly coming constructions.
It is submitted that the deceased was aged nineteen years and due to his untimely death, the family of the deceased is put to financial distress.
The tribunal has taken the income of the deceased only at Rs.20,000/- per month which is on the lower side and hence seeks indulgence of this Court.

Further, he submits that with regard to liability of insurance company is concerned, the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and absolutely there is no material to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the insurance company and sought for dismissal of the appeal preferred by the insurance and to suitably enhance the compensation.

In order to substantiate his submissions, the learned counsel relied upon the Division Bench judgment of this Court in the case of SRI RAMESH AND - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB ANOTHER v. NANDINI SHIVA AND OTHERS render in MFA No.102137 of 2014 decided on 18th January, 2016.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, we have examined the material placed before us.
PW1-D.P. Rudraiah who is petitioner No.1, reiterated averments made in the claim petition as to the accident and also produced documents.

Perusal of documents reveal that on the basis of complaint filed by D.P. Rudraiah, Molakalmuru Police registered a case in Crime No.3 of 2020 against the driver of the bus for the offence punishable under Section 279, 304A of Indian Penal Code and Sections 187, 3, 181, 146 and 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and submitted FIR to the Court.

Thereafter, Police have visited the spot, conducted spot panchanama and inquest panchanama in the presence of panchas, obtained MV report, Post-mortem report and recorded statement of witnesses and on investigation, filed charge sheet against the driver of the bus for offence punishable under Section 279 and 304A of Indian Penal Code and the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Investigating Officer has also filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for commission D P Rudraiah S/O Dodda Palaiah vs Alla Baksha S/O Sabjan Sab on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99900340/
6 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB of offence punishable under Section 3 read with 181 and Section 146 read with 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: RW1 has deposed in his evidence that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

He has clearly admitted in his evidence that, at the time of accident,
respondent No.1 was having the valid and effective driving licence and the insurance policy of the bus was in force.

Further, he admits that the charge-sheet is filed against the driver of the bus for rash and negligent act on his part and further he has stated that the insurance company is liable for payment of compensation as the policy was in force as on the date of accident and he has not been charge-sheeted before any court.

15. The main argument advanced on behalf of the insurance company is that the Investigating Officer has submitted charge sheet against the rider of motorcycle for commission of offence under Section 3 and 181 of Motor Vehicles Act, which clearly goes to show that the rider of the motorcycle was not having knowledge to ride the motorcycle and hence has contributed to the accident.
But the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB Investigating Officer has not made any accusation against the rider of the motorcycle as to rash and negligent act on his part.
Moreover the rider of the motorcycle was not having driving licence to ride the motorcycle and accident occurred only on the negligent act on the part of the rider of motorcycle.

In the absence of any cogent evidence placed by the insurance to substantiate its contention, the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and fastened the liability on the owner of offending vehicle, i.e. the bus.

On re-appreciation and re-examination of the entire evidence on record, we do not find any illegality/legal infirmity in the impugned judgment and award and the award passed by the Tribunal as to the liability of the Insurance Company.
Hence, we answer point No.1 in the negative.

16. As regards quantum of compensation is concerned, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimants submitted that the deceased was a B.Com final year student and because of the financial condition of the house, he was also doing work of water-curing to the newly coming-up buildings and was earning Rs.600/- per day and was contributing the same to his family.
This Court in the case of SRI RAMESH AND ANOTHER - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB (supra) has assessed the income of the deceased, who was a diploma student at Rs.20,000/- per month.
On the basis of the said judgment, the learned counsel for the claimants in this appeal also submits that the income has to be taken at Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioners have produced Exhibits P8 and P9, i.e. SSLC, PUC marks cards which reveal that he secured first class in SSLC and PUC; and Exhibits P10 to 13 are the B.Com degree certificates.

Except these documents, the claimants have not produced any other document to assess the income D P Rudraiah S/O Dodda Palaiah vs Alla Baksha S/O Sabjan Sab on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99900340/
7 of the deceased.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has also rightly observed that though the claimants have not produced any documents as to the income of the deceased, however, considering the decision of Delhi High Court in the case of RAJ BALA AND ANOTHER v. SUMIT DAHIYA AND OTHERS MAC App.462 of 2018 decided on 22nd October, 2018; and in the case of HDFC ERGO GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. RATTAN KUMAR DWIVEDI reported in 2017 SCC ONLINE DEL. 9874,
the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month.

entities.text: RAJ BALA AND ANOTHER v. SUMIT DAHIYA AND OTHERS MAC App.462 of 2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: HDFC ERGO GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. RATTAN KUMAR DWIVEDI reported in 2017 SCC ONLINE DEL. 9874
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Division Bench of this Court in the case of SRI RAMESH AND ANOTHER (supra), has also assessed the income of the deceased therein who was a diploma student,
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB has assessed the income at Rs.20,000/- per month.

Following the analogy of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of SRI RAMESH AND ANOTHER (supra),
considering the age and qualification of the deceased, it is just and proper to assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.18,000/- in the case on hand.
Accordingly it is taken.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% is to be added to the income towards future prospects.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the monthly income comes to Rs.25,200/-.
Since the deceased was a Bachelor, 50% is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
After deduction the monthly income would come to Rs.12,600/-.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case SARLA VERMA (SMT.) AND OTHERS v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER, reported in (2009)6 SCC 121, the appropriate multiplier to be applied is 18 and the same is adopted by the Tribunal.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA (SMT.) AND OTHERS v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER, reported in (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, the loss of dependency would come to Rs.27,21,600/-
(Rs.12,600/- x 12 x 18). Further, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of SARLA VERMA, in the case of PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB (supra), and in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. NANU RAM @ CHUHRU RAM AND OTHRS reported in (2018)18 SCC 130, the claimants are entitled for compensation as follows:
Sl.No. Head Amount (in Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 27,21,600.00  2. Loss of consortium (Rs.40,000 x 80,000.00  8)
 3. Loss of Estate 15,000.00  4. Towards transportation of dead 15,000.00  body and funeral expenses  Total 28,31,600.00

opennyai_summary.arguments:
11. Sri G.N. Raichur, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in saddling the liability on the Insurance in spite of the defence and evidence on record that the rider of motorcycle was riding the same without having driving licence and the motorcycle was also not insured.
It is also contended that the Tribunal has committed an error in taking the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month in spite of petitioners have not produced any documentary proof in support of the income.
The tribunal has taken the income of the deceased only at Rs.20,000/- per month which is on the lower side and hence seeks indulgence of this Court.
Further, he submits that with regard to liability of insurance company is concerned, the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and absolutely there is no material to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the insurance company and sought for dismissal of the appeal preferred by the insurance and to suitably enhance the compensation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Perusal of documents reveal that on the basis of complaint filed by D.P. Rudraiah, Molakalmuru Police registered a case in Crime No.3 of 2020 against the driver of the bus for the offence punishable under Section 279, 304A of Indian Penal Code and Sections 187, 3, 181, 146 and 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and submitted FIR to the Court.
Investigating Officer has also filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for commission D P Rudraiah S/O Dodda Palaiah vs Alla Baksha S/O Sabjan Sab on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99900340/
6 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB of offence punishable under Section 3 read with 181 and Section 146 read with 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
14.
15. The main argument advanced on behalf of the insurance company is that the Investigating Officer has submitted charge sheet against the rider of motorcycle for commission of offence under Section 3 and 181 of Motor Vehicles Act, which clearly goes to show that the rider of the motorcycle was not having knowledge to ride the motorcycle and hence has contributed to the accident.
But the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10953-DB Investigating Officer has not made any accusation against the rider of the motorcycle as to rash and negligent act on his part.
Moreover the rider of the motorcycle was not having driving licence to ride the motorcycle and accident occurred only on the negligent act on the part of the rider of motorcycle.
In the absence of any cogent evidence placed by the insurance to substantiate its contention, the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and fastened the liability on the owner of offending vehicle, i.e. the bus.
On re-appreciation and re-examination of the entire evidence on record, we do not find any illegality/legal infirmity in the impugned judgment and award and the award passed by the Tribunal as to the liability of the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal has also rightly observed that though the claimants have not produced any documents as to the income of the deceased, however, considering the decision of Delhi High Court in the case of RAJ BALA AND ANOTHER v. SUMIT DAHIYA AND OTHERS MAC App.462 of 2018 decided on 22nd October, 2018; and in the case of HDFC ERGO GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. RATTAN KUMAR DWIVEDI reported in 2017 SCC ONLINE DEL. 9874,
the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month.
Following the analogy of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of SRI RAMESH AND ANOTHER (supra),
considering the age and qualification of the deceased, it is just and proper to assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.18,000/- in the case on hand.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% is to be added to the income towards future prospects.

rpc_texts: Since the deceased was a Bachelor, 50% is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
